title: Integrating Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and SHAP Explainability to Predict Severe Acute Pancreatitis.
summary: A retrospective single-center cohort of 743 adults (67 severe cases) was used to predict severe acute pancreatitis from ED-arrival variables; the top RFE-RF+kNN pipeline had test-set AUROC 0.826.
ai_technology: Six feature selectors were combined with six ML classifiers; SHAP ranked variable contributions.
organization: Department of Emergency Medicine, Gönen State Hospital

evidence.tested: The best RFE-RF-feature+kNN pipeline predicted Revised Atlanta severe disease (AUROC 0.826; 95% CI 0.686–0.965) in the study cohort.
evidence.unknown: A retrospective single-center cohort of 743 adults (67 severe cases) was used to predict severe acute pancreatitis from ED-arrival variables; the top RFE-RF+kNN pipeline had test-set AUROC 0.826. A random 70/30 split was used, with five-fold training CV and performance on the independent internal 30% test set; bootstrap CIs and calibration were reported. Retrospective single-center results need external validation and do not establish improved outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: Six feature selectors were combined with six ML classifiers; SHAP ranked variable contributions.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
